body: In the middle of the arms race with the Soviet Union, the United States Air Force commissioned Lockheed to study a flying, nuclear-powered aircraft carrier. On September 12, 1969, G. Daniel Brewer, S. Dalton and P. J. Sibley submitted company report LR-22802, setting out the CL-1201 concept: a flying-wing design of nearly 6,000 tons with a wingspan of 1,120 feet, able to carry at least 22 fighter aircraft under its wings and cruise continuously for 41 days without resupply. There is no record that the Air Force ever ordered a real aircraft: no such order appears in the public files, including NASA memorandum X-2386. The CL-1201 never left the drawing board, but the study shows how far the idea of a flying aircraft carrier was taken.

The baseline design used a liquid-metal-cooled reactor rated at 1,830 megawatts of thermal power, driving four large tail-mounted turbofan engines to fly at Mach 0.8 at 30,000 feet, with the aim of ending dependence on overseas bases. The study also described a larger dual-loop atomic power plant rated at 5,470 megawatts, with liquid lithium circulating at about 1,093 degrees Celsius, fans 28 feet across, 300,000 pounds of thrust per engine and shielding weighing 1.2 million pounds. The idea had a troubled history: President Kennedy had already cancelled the aircraft nuclear power programme in 1961 because the problems of reactor safety and shielding could not be solved. The NB-36H had flown 47 test flights carrying an operating reactor, but the reactor and its shielding were too heavy, and intercontinental ballistic missiles and aerial refuelling had removed the strategic need for a nuclear-powered bomber.

The study defined two main variants. The CL-1201-1-1 was an attack carrier with a crew of 845 and 22 fighter aircraft embarked, while the CL-1201-1-3 was a logistics support variant able to move 3,896 troops and 6,207 tons of equipment. Recovering fighters in flight was one of the hardest problems: the design used a hydraulically stabilised hook extending 35 feet below the fuselage, which would engage a latch on the fighter's back before a winch pulled the aircraft into a maintenance bay. But turbulence beneath the wing and wingtip vortices moving at more than 120 feet per second would have endangered pilots, and the 560-foot tailless fuselage presented an enormous radar cross-section, easy for Soviet S-200 long-range air defence systems to detect hundreds of miles away. A single hit could have destroyed the entire embarked force at once and damaged the reactor.

Take-off was another problem with no good answer. At a gross weight of 11.85 million pounds, about 15 times a Boeing 747 or a C-5, no runway in the world could have borne the CL-1201, so the design turned to vertical take-off, with 182 jet-fuel turbine engines built in, each producing 90,000 pounds of thrust for a combined 16.38 million pounds. Firing them together would have produced downward exhaust at about 760 degrees Celsius, enough to damage concrete and asphalt runways, and a single five-minute take-off would have burned nearly 1.9 million pounds of JP-5 fuel, roughly the load of six fully laden C-5s. Synchronising 182 engines, and the asymmetric rolling moment if one failed, was a further major risk.

The idea itself was not new. In the 1930s the US Navy operated the rigid airships Akron and Macon, each 785 feet long and able to carry up to five Curtiss F9C-2 fighters, recovered in flight by an aerial trapeze. Akron was lost off New Jersey on April 4, 1933, and Macon off Point Sur, California, on February 12, 1935. The trapeze system itself never lost an aircraft during an in-flight recovery, but after Macon the Navy stopped developing flying aircraft carriers. The CL-1201 took the same concept and scaled it up to an almost unimaginable size, which is why it remains a Cold War curiosity rather than an aircraft that ever flew.
en.summary: In 1969 Lockheed proposed the CL-1201, a nuclear-powered flying aircraft carrier of nearly 6,000 tons that could carry 22 fighters and stay airborne for 41 days. Reactor weight, fighter recovery, radar visibility and a vertical take-off needing 182 engines kept it on the drawing board.
en.title: Lockheed's CL-1201 was a nuclear-powered flying aircraft carrier that never left the drawing board

facts.claim: The US Air Force commissioned Lockheed to study a flying nuclear-powered aircraft carrier; on September 12, 1969, G. Daniel Brewer, S. Dalton and P. J. Sibley submitted company report LR-22802 proposing the CL-1201.

The CL-1201 was a flying-wing design of nearly 6,000 tons with a 1,120-foot wingspan, able to carry at least 22 fighters under its wings and cruise for 41 days without resupply; no record shows the Air Force ordered a real aircraft, including in NASA memorandum X-2386.

The CL-1201-1-1 attack carrier variant had a crew of 845 and carried 22 fighters; the CL-1201-1-3 logistics variant could move 3,896 troops and 6,207 tons of equipment.

Fighter recovery used a hydraulically stabilised hook extending 35 feet below the fuselage, engaging a latch on the fighter's back before a winch pulled it into a maintenance bay; turbulence and wingtip vortices over 120 feet per second endangered pilots, and the 560-foot tailless fuselage was highly visible to Soviet S-200 air defences hundreds of miles away.

body: 在與蘇聯軍備競賽的背景下，美國空軍委託洛克希德進行一項飛行核動力航空母艦的工程研究。1969年9月12日，G. Daniel Brewer、S. Dalton與P. J. Sibley提交公司報告LR-22802，提出CL-1201構想：這是一架近6,000噸、翼展1,120英尺的飛翼設計，預計可在機翼下掛載至少22架戰鬥機，並連續巡航41天無須補給。目前沒有紀錄顯示美國空軍曾正式下訂實機，包含NASA備忘錄X-2386在內的公開檔案亦無此紀錄。CL-1201從未離開圖紙，但這份研究顯示，飛行航空母艦的構想曾被推進到多遠的地步。

基準設計採用液態金屬冷卻反應器，可提供1,830百萬瓦熱能，驅動4具大型尾部渦扇發動機，以0.8馬赫在30,000英尺高度飛行，目標是擺脫對海外基地的依賴。研究中另有一套額定5,470百萬瓦的雙迴路原子動力裝置設計，液態鋰在攝氏約1,093度下循環，風扇直徑達28英尺，每具發動機推力300,000磅，屏蔽重量達120萬磅。這個構想有著曲折的前史：甘迺迪總統已於1961年取消飛機核動力計畫，原因是無法解決反應器的安全與防護問題。NB-36H曾攜帶運作中的反應器進行47次試飛，但反應器與屏蔽過重，加上洲際彈道飛彈與空中加油的發展，使核動力轟炸機失去戰略必要性。

研究定義了兩種主要型號。CL-1201-1-1為攻擊型航空母艦，編制845人，搭載22架戰鬥機；CL-1201-1-3為後勤支援型，可運送3,896名士兵與6,207噸裝備。在空中回收戰鬥機是最困難的問題之一：設計使用可伸出機身下方35英尺的液壓穩定吊鉤，由戰鬥機背部鎖扣接合，再以絞盤拉入維修艙。但機翼下方的亂流與翼尖渦流速度可超過每秒120英尺，對飛行員構成危險；此外，560英尺長的無尾機身雷達截面極大，容易被蘇聯S-200等長程防空系統在數百英里外發現，一次命中可能同時摧毀整個機隊並損壞反應器。

起降是另一個沒有好答案的問題。CL-1201總重達1,185萬磅，約為波音747或C-5的15倍，全球沒有跑道能承受，因此改採垂直起降設計，內建182具噴射燃料渦輪發動機，每具推力90,000磅，合計1,638萬磅。同時點火會產生攝氏約760度的向下排氣，可能損壞混凝土與瀝青路面；單次5分鐘起飛程序即消耗近190萬磅JP-5燃料，相當於6架滿載C-5的油量。182具發動機同步運轉、以及其中一具熄火時的非對稱滾轉力矩，也構成重大風險。

這個構想本身並不新。1930年代，美國海軍操作硬式飛船阿克倫號（Akron）與梅肯號（Macon），兩艘飛船長785英尺，各可搭載最多5架Curtiss F9C-2戰鬥機，並以空中吊架回收。阿克倫號於1933年4月4日在紐澤西外海失事，梅肯號於1935年2月12日在加州Point Sur外海失事。吊架回收本身未曾在空中回收時損失飛機，但梅肯號失事後，海軍不再繼續發展飛行航空母艦。CL-1201把同樣的構想放大到幾乎難以想像的規模，也因此它始終只是冷戰時期的一件奇想，而非真正飛上天的飛機。
zh.summary: 1969年洛克希德提出CL-1201：一架近6,000噸的核動力飛行航空母艦，可搭載22架戰機、連續飛行41天。反應器重量、戰機回收、雷達可見度與需要182具發動機的垂直起降，讓它始終停留在圖紙上。
zh.title: 洛克希德CL-1201：核動力飛機的冷戰狂想——能載22架戰機卻從未離開圖紙
